basis: B-cell lymphoma; blood-cell lineage and lymphoma mechanism apply. No extranodal organ involvement is established as common.
Gastroschisis variant defined by an abdominal wall defect with herniation of abdominal viscera, typically bowel.
Fungal infection predominantly causing interstitial pneumonia; extrapulmonary infection is rare.
Benign vascular tumour arising in perineural tissues; vascular origin and nerve-associated location define the lesion.
Oral, digital/skeletal and CNS malformations define this subtype; cardiac septal hypertrophy is another defining feature, retained as the fourth axis.
Organic aciduria defined by optic atrophy and choreoathetosis; optic atrophy 10/10 and movement abnormalities 80-99%.
Postcholecystectomy biliary syndrome; the urinary-bladder parent is inconsistent with the definition. Abdominal symptoms alone do not establish additional organ damage.
Developmental delay 5/5 with skeletal defects; oral/GI abnormalities ~40-50%, stapes ankylosis 1/2 assessed. Cardiac and ocular findings omitted by cap; cohorts are small.
Histiocytic dermatoarthritis is characterized by cutaneous histiocytic lesions and destructive joint disease; no common additional organ damage established.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A2 does not justify adding skeletal manifestations from other syndromes.
Inherited corneal endothelial dystrophy with corneal opacity; confined to the ocular axis.
Inflammatory and fibrotic polyp of the colon. Associated inflammatory bowel disease is separate; local inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Tongue absence/hypoplasia defines disease; micrognathia and upper-airway obstruction each occur in 30-79%. Speech delay is mechanical; aspiration pneumonia is under 30%.
Pineal parenchymal malignancy arising within the CNS; no additional common organ damage established.
Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma of thymic origin; endocrine-cell lineage supports this axis. Thymic location alone does not establish immune dysfunction.
Tick-borne viral CNS infection; encephalitis is the defining disease localization despite many infections remaining non-neurologic. Hearing and visual sequelae are under 30%.
Inherited renal water-excretion defect causing hypotonic hyponatremia. Acute electrolyte-related seizures and elevated blood pressure do not establish lasting extra-organ damage.
Umbrella disease of the auditory system; no additional organ axis applies across the group.
Tyrosine metabolism disorder umbrella including transient neonatal cases; hepatic/renal injury chiefly type I and ocular/skin disease type II are not common across the whole group.
MELAS is a mitochondrial metabolic encephalomyopathy defined by lactic acidosis, cerebral stroke-like episodes and skeletal myopathy; genotype alone adds no organs.
Defined by skeletal muscle volume loss and atrophy. Peripheral nerve disease causes only a subset and is not required across this umbrella.
Inherited ventricular rhythm disorder; ventricular tachycardia and conduction abnormalities involve the heart.
Brain/renal malformations define syndrome; marrow failure and Peters anomaly each 1/1 assessed. Pulmonary hypoplasia omitted by cap and possible oligohydramnios effect; sparse data.
Classic eosinophilic pustular folliculitis is a sterile, immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation of skin follicles; no common systemic organ damage established.
Inherited transport disorder defined by cataract/microcornea, each 11/14, and renal glucosuria, 9/14; no other renal tubular defects described.
